prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Native game character ACTION sprite sheet, not an effects sheet.
Images 1 and 2: approved Daoist Q HD hand-painted finish references only, no UI/scenery/text. Image 3: exact Qingqi fish identity master. Image 4: approved eight-frame SWIM sheet for this exact fish and the required 4x2 animation grid, body size, detailed scale/gold trim and proportions. Now create its CAPTURE/HIT-STRUGGLE animation in eight genuinely different anatomical poses. The fish remains complete and visible through the last pose; game removes it after frame 7. No net or magic FX is needed.
Make a wide true-alpha 2:1 PNG, exactly FOUR equal square columns and TWO rows. Exactly one right-facing fish per cell, row-major order. Use SMALL detailed fish occupying central 62 percent of cell width; a full fish approximately 300px wide in an approx 1774x887 sheet. Same visible head/body SCALE as image 4, never enlarge fish. Leave minimum 15% truly transparent blank space on EVERY side of EVERY cell, including all tail and fine fin tips. Nothing crosses or touches a cell boundary. No grid lines, labels, numbers, background or shadow.
Identity: identical cobalt/cyan overlapping scales, white belly, amber-gold round eye with black pupil, gold cheek spiral and gold fin trim, broad translucent turquoise forked/fan tail, flowing blue fins. Preserve specific cheek and head markings, eye/mouth sizes and friendly rounded shape. Side view facing RIGHT always. Lock head and gill center within each cell, front body scale constant; only real tail/body/fin anatomical bends make the action. Keep eye visible for registration, expression can look startled then subdued.
Capture one-shot eight poses:
0: brief normal swimming entry pose matching first swim frame.
1: impact startle: mouth slightly opens, tail flares open, both paired fins spread outward by their joints.
2: strong first struggle: flexible rear body bends upward into a gentle C, tail folds upward/forward, near fin pulls inward and far fin extends.
3: counter struggle: rear body flexes down with tail fan folding the opposite way, near fin extends and far fin retracts.
4: second shorter struggle: tail is tightly curved up, pectorals raised with clearly changed membrane shapes, head stable.
5: fatigue: tail uncurls halfway downward, dorsal/ventral fins droop and pectorals fold closer.
6: settling: tail folds downward softly, fins partially collapse, less body tension.
7: subdued final captured pose: fish still right-facing and complete, open visible eye, tail loosely folded with relaxed narrow fins. Not a duplicate of any earlier frame. No final dissolve, fading, particles or shrinking.
Every frame must show actual alternate tail/fins/posterior-body silhouette and membrane shape changes with coherent anatomy. Do NOT just move, rotate, scale, mirror or squash the whole fish, and do not merely recolor or change glow. Preserve steady head position, consistent body size, camera and art style. Render clean true transparent RGBA, normal smooth antialiasing with no colored flecks or halos, high detail delicate golden borders, no water, bubbles, scenery, UI, painted checkerboard, text or added objects.
